result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers find the same core problems with similar, plausible contrast figures, and both offer warm replacement palettes. B is more specific: it measures primary against secondary and links against body text, calls the unreadable body text the biggest cause of the tired look, and offers an olive fallback for the primary in case olive is part of the brand. A is solid but more generic in its role analysis and less explicit about which fix to make first. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers find the roughly 1.7:1 contrast between body text and background, and their contrast figures check out. Both suggest a cream background, dark brown text and a green primary that keep the warm feel. B wins narrowly because it explains the muddiness with actual hue, saturation and lightness ranges and sets out the problems in a clear order. A's strengths are directly comparing the primary and secondary buttons (about 1.1:1) and offering an olive primary for keeping the brand hue, but it explains less of why the palette looks muddy.
